name: Grow a sourdough starter
blurb: Flour and water, left to catch wild yeast and bacteria. Most failures are impatience: there is a false rise around day two that fools nearly everyone.
gear: Wholemeal or rye flour to start, then strong white
steps: Mix 50 g wholemeal flour and 50 g water in a jar, cover loosely and leave somewhere warm.
Expect vigorous bubbling around day two — this is usually the wrong bacteria, and it will die back. Keep going.
From day three, discard all but about 25 g and feed with equal weights of flour and water, once or twice daily.
Watch for the real signs of maturity: a predictable rise and fall, a pleasant sour-yoghurt smell, and doubling within four to six hours of feeding.
Test with the float test: a spoonful of ripe starter should float in water.
Once it doubles reliably, bake with it, and settle into a maintenance rhythm — fridge storage with weekly feeds is fine.
tips: Days three to five are the discouraging dead zone. Almost everyone who quits, quits here.
Cold kitchens slow everything down. Find a warm spot around 24 °C.
Chlorinated tap water can inhibit it. Leave water out overnight or filter it.
proof: A starter that reliably doubles in four to six hours and raises a loaf without commercial yeast.
